newsitem.title: UK: Wool supply could rise 3.0 pct during 1996/7 -IWTO.
newsitem.headline: Wool supply could rise 3.0 pct during 1996/7 -IWTO.

text.p: World wool supplies could rise by around three percent to 1.68 million tonnes during 1996/97, according to the International Wool Textile Organisation (IWTO).
But despite improved trade clearances by major wool producers and increased sales from growers' holdings, "the wool market remains fundamentally oversupplied" the IWTO said in a published report.

Australia and New Zealand both saw substantial growth in wool exports during the first five months of the 1996/97 season. Australian exports rose by 25 percent year-on-year for the period, while New Zealand increased by 11 percent.
Western European and Pacific region order levels were also showing signs of improvement, the IWTO said, but added that wool prices were unlikely to respond until European yarn stocks were cleared.
New clip supplies were expected to contract by a further 30,000 tonnes to a postwar low of 1.47 million tonnes clean, the IWTO report said.
The clip supply carryforward would total some 241,000 tonnes clean, representing a leap of around 43 percent from 1995/96 levels.

The IWTO put global merino supplies at 764,000 tonnes for 1996/97, up around six percent on the previous year. But supplies for crossbred and carpet types would remain static at around 412,000 tonnes and 507,000 tonnes respectively, it said.

The market share for both crossbred and carpet types would consequently be 0.7 of a percentage point lower than last season, at 24.5 percent and 30.1 percent respectively. -Simon Gardner - London Newsroom + 44 171 542 8057
